html:
SMTO-PRX-0013 — Proxmox finished, but the VM isn't in the state you asked for

GUID: c6518e93-0615-4d5a-9b80-cc37ae42d9fe
Slug: proxmox-verification-failed
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • Proxmox reported the job as done, but when SMTO checked the VM afterwards it wasn't in the state you asked for, for example still running after a stop.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to show the VM's current status, without asking it to change anything. The VM may just be slow to reach the new state, for example still shutting down.
  2. In the Proxmox web interface, check the VM's Task History for anything else that acted on it, such as another person, a schedule or high availability. Another action on the same VM can undo or override yours.
  3. Only if the VM is still not in the state you want and nothing else is acting on it, ask for the action again. Repeating too soon can cause a second restart or stop.

What success looks like

  • The VM's status shows the state you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Proxmox server. Don't keep repeating the action while something else may be controlling the VM.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • After the Proxmox task stopped with exitstatus OK, a fresh guest status read did not show the requested target power state.

What this means

  • After a task reports completion, fresh guest status differs from the requested target power state. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • After a task reports completion, fresh guest status differs from the requested target power state.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact UPID, requested action and observed post-task guest state, including possible concurrent changes.

How to fix it

  • Compare state_after in the error facts with the action's target state, then read current guest status and the node task log for the UPID. Check for HA-managed resources, guest shutdown behavior or concurrent tasks before reporting completion or repeating the mutation.
  • Inspect authoritative live guest and task state before reporting completion or repeating a mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Authoritative guest/task evidence establishes the final state before further mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
